p: Little Woodham is set in the 1640s, a turbulent time on the eve of the English Civil War, and the villagers often weave the news and worries of the day into their chat. Ask about the King and Parliament and you'll get an earful, as well as a fascinating sense of how rumours spread when there was no telly or phone to rely on. It's a great way for older children to get their heads round a period that can feel a bit dry in the classroom.

As the village is run by a small team of volunteers, opening days are limited and can change, so double-check before you make the trip. That makes it a lovely thing to build a Gosport day around rather than a place to drop into on a whim.

The town itself is a goldmine for anyone interested in history, especially the navy. The Royal Navy Submarine Museum lets you climb aboard a real submarine, HMS Alliance, while Explosion, the museum of naval firepower, tells the story of the weapons that defended the fleet. Both are part of the National Museum of the Royal Navy, so you could easily spend a full day on naval history alone.

For fresh air, Stokes Bay has a long seafront with views across to the Isle of Wight, perfect for a stroll, a picnic or watching the ships come and go. And the little Gosport Ferry carries passengers across the harbour mouth to Portsmouth, where Gunwharf Quays and the historic dockyard await, so you can mix the 1600s with a modern waterfront in a single day.
